speaker: Renata Kallosh
title: Quantum gravity, higher-spin indices and superselfduality
summary: The actual new talk begins on P000841 and ends on P000842. Kallosh reports on the Cambridge relativity meeting, then describes higher-spin zero-mode formulae and self-dual supergravity. P000840 is a carry-in from the preceding notebook material: its vertex-model, Yang--Baxter and Ising observations were already indexed as 1978-460.12--20. They are preserved as provenance, not reassigned to Kallosh or duplicated as 1979 occurrences. The catalogue page interval is retained verbatim. The programme of a superspace index theorem is distinguished from the concrete index computations and from any claim of unrestricted ultraviolet finiteness.

speaker: V. E. Zakharov
title: Degenerate dispersion laws, resonances and integrability
summary: The talk begins on P000843, after Kallosh's report. Zakharov studies additional additive functions on wave-resonance manifolds, difference-curve parametrizations, dressing and a necessary resonance test for extra Hamiltonian integrals. Arnold connects this with translation surfaces, Poincaré obstructions and formal Birkhoff normal form. The subsequent programme appears in Zakharov--Schulman (1980, 1988) and the later Balk--Ferapontov web classification (1994); one additional collision invariant and infinitely many are distinct hypotheses. None of these statements identifies every notion of nonlinear integrability with degenerate scalar dispersion. P000847 ends with Gelfand's reading programme.

speaker: I. M. Gelfand
title: Spinors, quaternions and the Dirac equation
summary: P000848 contains Gelfand's introductory discussion of spinors, the projective action of two-component vectors, Hamilton's square-root idea and physical consequences of the Dirac theory. The quaternion conclusion requires an extra quotient relation: three anticommuting square roots of minus one alone generate a Clifford algebra. Kallosh's subsequent programme begins at the foot of the same page.

speaker: Renata Kallosh
title: Spinor calculus and gravitational index theorems
summary: The eight-part programme on P000848 is followed on P000849--P000853 by two-spinor calculus, self-duality, Laplace-type operators, heat coefficients and higher-spin spectral pairings. The notes themselves correct a proposed interpretation of the nonzero-mode term as a common eigenvalue multiplicity. They also contain incompatible numerical versions of an index formula on P000841 and P000853; these are recorded without silently repairing an unverified normalization. The dated heading on P000854 starts the next meeting.

speaker: I. M. Gelfand
title: Reading programme and exercises
summary: The actual contribution is the opening of P000854: a reading programme and exercises on Gaussian and quartic Fourier integrals and on self-adjoint operators for a symplectic form. The exercises are definite mathematical items, although the contribution is primarily a programme. Their solutions must distinguish the self-adjoint relation for an alternating form from the Hamiltonian, skew-adjoint relation.

speaker: S. G. Gindikin
title: Twistors and the conformal compactification of Minkowski space
summary: Starting on P000854, Gindikin describes the Hermitian space of signature (2,2), its two-plane Grassmannian, tube domains, the real Minkowski chart and null incidence. This continues the geometry of 1978-455.1. The manuscript's unrestricted affine chart stabilizer includes dilations, and its final point/ray correspondence interchanges the two sides of the twistor incidence relation. The higher-dimensional challenge is a programme, not a unique conjecture.

speaker: F. A. Berezin
title: Grassmann algebra, supermatrices and classification problems
summary: The dated lecture begins on P000859 and ends with two explicit matrix problems at the top of P000862. Gelfand proposes graph analogues of the even Grassmann algebra; Gindikin then recalls the BGG description of projective bundles and asks for actual maps and a Grassmannian counterpart. The repeated-body-spectrum problem is separated from the odd-entry commutant problem. Finite coefficient algorithms solve the literal finite-dimensional computational tasks; this chapter examines what additional structural information they provide.

speaker: G. B. Shabat
title: Double translation hypersurfaces and the Lie--Wirtinger theorem
summary: The contribution starts at the bottom of P000862 and ends midway down P000863. The catalogue names G. B. Shabat; the manuscript initial looks like \ru{Ю.}, a retained attribution discrepancy. The discussion explains the theta-divisor example and reports the classical converse, followed by Gelfand's broad integrability speculation. Genericity and the distinction between smooth Jacobians, generalized Jacobians and degenerations are indispensable.

speaker: Raphael Høegh-Krohn
title: Energy representations of current groups and Brownian paths
summary: The actual talk occupies the lower part of P000863 and P000864--P000865, translated by Gelfand. It constructs the energy representation, states irreducibility in dimension at least three, asks about dimension two and explains the one-dimensional Brownian realization. The name bears a question mark in the notebook but is identified by the catalogue. The construction needs a Gaussian realization outside the Hilbert space and a consistent Maurer--Cartan convention. A later claimed proof in every dimension cannot settle the two-dimensional question: the primary literature explicitly identifies a gap.
